parts.text:
Describe two behaviourist applications to learning.

Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about special educational needs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Every person is a unique individual, particularly in relation to their educational needs.
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about special educational needs and include a
discussion about individual differences.

Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe one theory of emotional intelligence.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest how you would test the reliability and validity of an emotional intelligence test.

text: Intelligence is measured with an intelligence test resulting in an IQ score. A test of emotional
intelligence produces an EQ score.

parts.text: Describe two study skills that could improve learning effectiveness.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would investigate which study skill is the more effective for your students.

Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Imagine you are a teacher. Your students are sitting the examination very soon and you want to
help them improve their learning effectively. You decide to try out two study skills to see which is
the more effective.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘improving adherence’ to medical requests.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two ways in which practitioner style can improve adherence to medical requests.
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about health and safety.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Psychological studies of health and safety may be interesting, but their usefulness is
questionable. Evaluate what psychologists have learned about health and safety including a
discussion of the usefulness of what has been found. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe one study which has used the fear arousal technique.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest a fear arousal strategy that could be used to promote health in relation to a specific
problem.

text: There are many specific health problems that are targeted by governments. But do they always
use the correct method to promote health?

parts.text:

whether the pain of the long-stay patients is reducing.

parts.label: (b)

Psychology and Environment
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Jamal is a nurse who works in a hospital looking after long-stay patients who have pain following a
major accident.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two events where it is known that survivors have suffered from post traumatic stress
disorder. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about environmental cognition.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Our cognitive map is the image we have in our head. But there are different ways to study that
image. Evaluate what psychologists have learned about environmental cognition and include
a discussion of the methods used to study environmental cognition. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe a study of community environmental design.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest how you would adapt such studies to your local area.

text: It has been decided to convert your local area into an ‘Americanised public place’ using community
environmental design and you are going to help.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe psychological features that make noise annoying.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would measure how annoying the noise is. 
Psychology and Abnormality
Section A
Answer this question.

text: People who live close to you make too much noise and it is annoying you. You know that sound is
measured in decibels, but you want to measure exactly how annoying the noise is.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by the term ‘obsessive-compulsive disorder’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Using an example, describe what is meant by a compulsion. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about phobias.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Some psychologists argue that phobias are learned just like any other behaviour. Evaluate
what psychologists have discovered about phobias and include a discussion of the
behaviourist explanation of phobias. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the main features of rational emotive therapy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how rational emotive therapy could be used to help students suffering from
examination stress.

text: Ellis (1962) outlined Rational Emotive Therapy to treat depression, but he also believed it could
help reduce stress.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the characteristics of addiction such as those outlined by Griffiths (1995).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how the characteristics of addiction apply to your son’s behaviour. 
Psychology and Organisations
Section A
Answer this question.

text: You are a parent and recently your seventeen-year-old son has started to behave differently from
usual.You have had money taken from your bag and you are concerned that he might be gambling.
You are worried that he might become addicted to it.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘selection interview’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe structured and unstructured selection interviews. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about group behaviour in organisations.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“If it applies to most people most of the time, then we need know nothing more.” Evaluate
what psychologists have discovered about group behaviour in organisations and include a
discussion of the issue of generalisations. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest an appropriate non-monetary reward for your workers. Give reasons for your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how rewards fit into one theory of motivation.

text: The workers in your organisation deserve a reward because they have been working hard. You
don’t want to pay them extra because you believe that there is more to life than money. You decide
to give them a number of non-monetary rewards.

parts.text: Describe one rapid rotating shift system.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest an alternative shift system that is likely to reduce human error. Give reasons for your
answer.

text: Both the Chernobyl (1986) and Three Mile Island (USA, 1979) nuclear power station accidents
were caused by human error. Workers were on a rapid rotating shift system, specifically the
‘graveyard’ 10pm until 6am shift when the accidents happened. If you were the manager of such
an organisation you would implement a very different shift system.
